note: The long walkthrough's voice copy: one line a shot, chapter by chapter (docs/demo/walkthrough.md is the master). 'say' is what the voice reads when it differs from the caption.

lines.text: Xenoform turns a song into a music video. One object turns into the next, on the beat, for the whole song.
It runs on your own computer, with open-weight models through ComfyUI. This is the whole tour: the song, the vibe, what it morphs through, the render, the edit, your own clips, and how it's built.
Start with a song. Drop a file on the page, or use the bundled demo.
The desk listens first. It finds the beats, the bars and the drop, and tells you where the big moment is. That's where the biggest change will land.
Then pick a vibe. A vibe is what everything is made of and how it's lit: molten gold, neon noir, ink and paper, deep-sea glow, and more.
Each vibe brings its own objects, its own colour and its own transitions. Pick None for the things as they really are, in their own materials and plain light.
Under the vibes is one line: what it morphs through. It isn't a story prompt. It names the things you want to see.
Type a few things, a theme, a place, or a feel. A theme like racing brings fifteen things of its own: a rally car, a helmet, a trophy, a chequered flag.
A place becomes a scene the morphs pass through. A feel, like moody and punchy, moves the knobs and the look.
The chips under the line show how it was read. New means Make draws that still first, on your GPU, before it renders.
The objects come from a library that grows on this machine. Every still is made with Z-Image Turbo and checked against the vibe's own pool before it's kept.
Press Make. The making screen shows the chain it picked, the steps, and a rough cut of the song playing while the morphs render.
You can leave it. The tab counts up and tells you when it's ready.

There are three models. A Draft renders small with LTX-Video, in minutes. A Fast Final upscales the Draft to 1080p. The Final renders every morph with LTX-2.3: sharp, and slow, a few minutes a morph on this card.
lines.say: There are three models. A Draft renders small with LTX Video, in minutes. A Fast Final upscales the Draft to ten eighty p. The Final renders every morph with LTX 2.3: sharp, and slow, a few minutes a morph on this card.

lines.text: The time row says how long it will take on this GPU, before you start.

Now the engine. Morph style is how one object becomes the next. Melt flows. Shatter cracks into shards that snap together. Bloom opens like a flower. Spin turns as it changes. Fold creases like paper. Auto melts the verses and shatters the drop.
Timing is when the change happens inside the shot. Smooth plays it evenly. On the beat moves it in steps, on every beat. Snap holds, then changes in about a beat, on the downbeat.
Effects ride the kick and the loudness: dither hits, a feedback tunnel, a kaleidoscope, slit-scan. Any of them together.
Foreshadow lets the next object arrive early: its edges glow in, or strips of it flicker toward the cut. Scenes mixes wide places in at each new section.
And four knobs. Intensity for the pulse and the flash, Speed for how often it cuts, Chaos for the punches, Glow for the bloom.
None of this needs the GPU again. Every change waits in one bar at the bottom, and Apply re-cuts the video from the morphs it already made.
Under the video is the timeline. Every tile is a shot, with its own frame, and a playhead crosses it as the video plays.
Click a shot to open it. The drawer has four tabs.
Shot: play it, move it left or right, duplicate it, or delete it. The shot before plays on through the gap.
Look: colour for this shot alone, hue, saturation, brightness, contrast and warmth, and its own effects.
Join: the seam between two shots. Flow or cut, the transition, and move the cut a beat or half a beat either way.
Regenerate: swap the object, change its morph style, render just this one morph again, or generate a new one here.
Edit as many shots as you like, then apply once. It re-cuts from the cached morphs, without the GPU.
Morph has a second mode: your clips. Point it at a folder of your own film, and the cut is only your footage, never mixed with objects.
Each clip plays its busiest stretch, at full speed. Between clips, LTX generates a morph from the last frame of one into the first frame of the next.
Here, The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari turns into Nosferatu, and Nosferatu into NASA archive footage. All public domain.

lines.text: When it's done, share it: a small share cut, a fifteen-second hook for social, or the whole thing.
Edit in Resolve opens a folder with a timeline: one file a shot, the song, and markers, ready to import.
A recipe code remakes the same video anywhere. And Variations queues extra Drafts for later: new objects, other vibes, other feels.
How it's built. The song is split into stems with Demucs, and analysed for beats, bars and the drop.
The plan becomes ComfyUI graphs, sent through the Comfy SDK to your own ComfyUI. LTX-Video, LTX-2.3 and Z-Image Turbo do the work: all open weights, on one 12 GB card.

lines.text: And an MCP server lets any AI drive the desk: pick a vibe, render, review, and re-cut.
Setup and models checks your machine, and downloads any model it lacks.
